answer: The papermaker dips his mould in the vat only when the pulp is beaten fine, and the stationer pays by the ream after the sheets are pressed. Osteopath registration with osteopathy council attestation is the watermark pressed into every sheet: four-year degree, 1,000 clinical hours, registration exam, annual renewal. A ream made from a borrowed spiral cockles in the damp and will not take ink. The jade is the refund, the paper's price and the printer's day both lost, and the jetty is the vat book, kept by the master papermaker and shown to every stationer.
